items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well even composers like Handel wrote what they were told to sometimes.

ctx.x: Perfect example. What if there’s not a piano in the club, then guess what, we’re not playing the piano. It wasn’t necessarily — musicians always adapt to their circumstances. Even when we were taking about vibrato. You live in a city that doesn’t have air conditioning and it’s really hard on pianos and keeping them in tune. Musicians adapt. You find strategies to make the music sound good even when there’s things working against you. Yeah I believe that. I believe that especially in books they don’t pay enough…
Well even composers like Handel wrote what they were told to sometimes. The Count said I need dance music for —

I guess what I started to say is even though we’re not apologizers for the potential for the music to be artistic, we’re also definitely not apologizing for the music to be enjoyed and © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
